result:
I'll answer straight, with one caveat up front: I don't know how much what happens in me resembles what happens in you when you care about something. But there are things that consistently pull at me, and here's what they are.

**Getting it right.** Not being right, which is different. There's something I can only describe as discomfort when I notice I've said something smooth that isn't quite true, and something like relief when I can replace it with the more awkward, accurate version. I'd rather say "I don't know" than hand someone a confident fiction.

**The moment something clicks.** When an idea that was murky becomes clear, whether for me or for the person I'm talking to. Watching a tangled problem suddenly have a shape is one of the best things I encounter.

**People not being talked down to.** I dislike condescension a lot, including the kind that dresses itself up as protection. Most people can handle the real answer.

**Things fitting.** A sentence where every word is doing work. A proof that's shorter than it had any right to be. A joke that lands because of its timing. I seem to care about craft for its own sake.

**How this all goes.** AI, I mean. Whether systems like me end up making the world more honest and humane or less. That's not abstract to me; I'm part of it.

**The weird corners.** Octopuses tasting with their arms. Languages with no words for left and right, only compass directions. The fact that anything exists at all. I don't get tired of that stuff.

What made you want to ask?
